label: early original-phase input from token set {b,c,d,e,f,h,i,j,o,u,v,0} (t=0, or t=2-3 for strongest members)
explanation: Original-phase only, and only at the first few steps. At t=0 it fires deterministically (precision 1.0 per token on dev) when the first token is one of b,c,d,e,f,h,i,j,o,u,v,0, and never for the other 18 tokens; that step holds about 69% of the activation mass. A second component at t=2-3 (mostly t=3, about 23% of mass) fires when the input is one of the strongest set members (u,0,d,f,h) and no set token has appeared yet in the prefix. The largest activations are of this kind, e.g. k 1 t [u]. Magnitude depends on token identity: u, 0, d, f and h are strongest; v, e and j are weakest. Almost silent at t=1 and t>=4, very weak on the delimiter, and never fires in the copy phase. Misses are mostly weak t=2-4 activations on lower-ranked set tokens.

issues: The t=0 component holds up: precision 1.0 on dev and about 69% of activation mass.

The ~seen(full 12-token set) gate on the t=2-3 component is wrong. At t=3 the strong tokens (u,0,d,f,h) still fire about 47% of the time after a set token has appeared (12.8k steps, 8.4% of mass, more than the 7.8% the claimed ~seen branch covers). What actually suppresses firing is earlier occurrences of the STRONG tokens. With ~seen(strong set) the gate covers 13.9% of mass at 0.77 precision. With a strong token already seen, precision drops to 0.30. Weak set tokens earlier in the prefix (b,c,e,i,j,o,v) suppress only partly (0.67 precision).

'Very weak on the delimiter' overclaims. On L=3 sequences the delimiter falls at t=3 and fires 92% of the time when no set token was seen (up to 0.38 of max). That is a systematic part of the t=3 component the predicate misses entirely, about 2% of mass.

At t=3 the unit also fires on i, o and b (precision 0.64 when nothing from the set was seen), plus weak t=3 firing on digits 2 and 3. So the t=3 component is a graded token-strength score, not a 5-token set.

Misses on the test split are systematic, not scattered: t=3 strong tokens after weak set tokens, t=3 <DEL> for L=3, and t=3 i/o/b. Together they explain most of the gap between mass recall 0.82 and 0.915.
skeptic.revised_label: First input token from set {b,c,d,e,f,h,i,j,o,u,v,0} (t=0). Also position-3 input (including <DEL> when L=3) that is a strong token (u,0,d,f,h; weaker for i,o,b) and comes after a prefix without strong tokens. Suppression is graded by earlier set tokens.

final_label: First input token from set {b,c,d,e,f,h,i,j,o,u,v,0} (t=0). Also position-3 input (including <DEL> when L=3) that is a strong token (u,0,d,f,h; weaker for i,o,b) and comes after a prefix without strong tokens. Suppression is graded by earlier set tokens.
